## Gate 1: pre-push integration-suite hook

**What I found:** The one-week trial ended on 10 September with no decision and no measurement, so the integration suite has been missing from pre-push for about eleven weeks. Turn the gate back on (the record calls this REINSTATE). That is the default for any trial that expires without a decision, and nobody ever measured the 5% red-rate criterion.

**Why it matters:** Every push since 10 September has skipped a check that nobody decided to remove, and the "trial until 10 September" comment makes it look like someone is managing it. Changing the date now would extend the suspension without a decision. Doing nothing keeps the hook disabled indefinitely.

**Do this first:**
1. Restore the integration-suite call in the pre-push hook and delete the "trial until 10 September" comment in the same change.
2. Follow-up: if someone still wants the trial, pull the suite's CI red rate for 3–10 September from CI history. A new TRIAL is allowed only if it cites that data, names an owner, and has a dated CI step that fails once the new expiry passes.
3. Follow-up: add a negative control. A known-failing integration test, run through the hook, must stop the push.

**What I did not check:** the hook file and the CI history. I didn't open the repo; everything here comes from your description. Measuring the red rate needs your CI's run-history query for that suite over 3–10 September.

```text
Gate:         pre-push hook running the integration suite (developer machines)
Stage:        pre-push (local)
Trigger:      suspended (expiry 10 September passed, undecided)
Proof:        UNPROVEN (no recorded negative control or last red)
Scope:        declared integration suite on push / effective none / delta whole suite unchecked at pre-push since 3 September
Baseline:     none
Status:       TRIAL (expired)
Decision:     REINSTATE
Guard:        hook blocks again and a known-failing integration test turns it red
Handoff:      none (a renewed TRIAL comes back here with measured 3–10 September data)
Next action:  restore the suite call in the pre-push hook; remove the stale trial comment
Verification: Not run. No repo access; run the hook against a deliberately failing integration test and confirm the push is refused.
```

## Gate 2: deploy gate

**What I found:** The deploy gate failed at authentication with "application identifier not found in the directory" before it compared anything against the target environment. That means it couldn't evaluate, not that it found a defect. Keep it blocking, label the run as unable to evaluate, fix the identity, and prove it with a deliberate failure (the record calls the status INDETERMINATE and the decision PROVE). The proposal to delete it rests on two things that don't justify removal: today's error, and a gate that has never fired, which makes it unproven rather than useless.

**Why it matters:** Deleting it would remove the only comparison against the target environment, and nothing would show whether it ever could have caught anything. Leaving the auth error unexplained means it keeps reading as a red result, which feeds the case for deleting it.

**Do this first:**
1. Find out why the gate's identity no longer resolves. Typical causes are a deleted or rotated app registration, a wrong tenant or directory ID in the pipeline variables, or a service principal that was never created in that directory. Restore it.
2. Follow-up: give identity, tooling or environment failures their own exit code or label, separate from "violation found".
3. Follow-up: add a negative control, for example deploying against a target with known drift, that must turn the gate red. Then record that run.

**What I did not check:** which identity provider and pipeline config the gate uses, and its run history. A sign-in-log query in the directory for that application ID will show when it stopped resolving.

```text
Gate:         deploy gate (compares against target environment; runs in deploy pipeline)
Stage:        deploy (needs target-environment state)
Trigger:      indeterminate (IdP: application identifier not found in directory)
Proof:        UNPROVEN ("not catching real defects" = never seen red on a defect)
Scope:        declared target-environment comparison / effective none this run / delta comparison not executed
Baseline:     none
Status:       INDETERMINATE
Decision:     PROVE
Guard:        negative control runs in CI, or its last red run is recorded
Handoff:      defect-shift-left (8a: gate depends on target-environment state); functionality-complexity-tradeoff only if someone argues the obligation itself is gone
Next action:  restore the gate's application identity in the directory and give evaluation failures a distinct exit code
Verification: Not run. No repo or IdP access; rerun the gate after the identity fix, then run it against a known-drifted target and confirm it goes red.
```

Retiring the deploy gate would need evidence that it can't currently meet: either what it checks is gone, a proven gate covering the same scope catches it earlier, or the obligation was retired.
